Topline data from the Phase 1b/2 TUPELO study of REC-4881 4 mg once daily, including the expanded adult (18+) FAP population (data cutoff: September 10, 2026): - Total GI tract : After 12 weeks of treatment, 87% of patients (13 of 15) had reductions in total polyp burden, with a 47% median reduction - 1 in 3 patients (5 of 15) achieved a reduction of 65% or more - At Week 25, after a 12-week off-treatment follow-up, 85% (11 of 13) were still below baseline - Upper GI tract : After 12 weeks of treatment, 92% of patients had reductions in upper GI polyp burden - Nearly half (6 of 13) achieved a reduction of 65% or more - Two patients achieved a reduction of ≥98% polyp burden reduction in the upper GI - 50% (6 of 12) improved by at least one Spigelman stage at Week 13 - At Week 25, after a 12-week off-treatment follow-up, 92% (11 of 12) were still below baseline - Favorable safety profile supports potential for chronic dosing: No TRAEs above Grade 3 were observed.
Additional Phase 1 monotherapy data are expected in the second half of 2026, and preliminary dose expansion data in endometrial cancer are expected in the second half of 2027.
